question:
A recurring workflow in our team passes work from one person to the next, and today only two senior developers know how it goes. I want to write it down so that new developers and automated coding agents follow it the same way every time: what must the write-up state, and in what forms can it be written?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

A recurring handoff workflow must be written down so that any developer or automated agent can follow it consistently. The write-up must specify required inputs, transforming activities, and outputs for each step, clarify roles and responsibilities, record design rationale, and be expressed in a form understandable to its audience—using natural language, diagrams, or formal notations.

# Guidelines

- The write-up must describe required inputs, transforming activities, and outputs generated at each step, since [SWEBOK excerpt 24f5a67c87fc0b0f7a43]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Engineering Processes, Lifecycles, and Measurement/Software Engineering Processes and System Lifecycles/Software Engineering Process Definition and Structure/Software Process Definition and Components.md)

- The write-up must be easy to understand and correct, because process specifications are the basis for coordination, agreement, measurement, and quality management. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Engineering Processes, Lifecycles, and Measurement/Software Processes and Life Cycle Management/Software Process Definition and Life Cycle Specification.md)

- [SWEBOK excerpt 3d38e79e462547e07bb3]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Engineering Processes, Lifecycles, and Measurement/Software Processes and Life Cycle Management/Software Process Definition and Life Cycle Specification.md)

- The write-up must also include controls such as directives and constraints, and enabling mechanisms such as tools, technologies, or resources. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Engineering Processes, Lifecycles, and Measurement/Software Engineering Processes and System Lifecycles/Software Engineering Process Definition and Structure/Software Process Definition and Components.md)

- Procedures should [SWEBOK excerpt c284d7a5887b0100847a], with roles and responsibilities made clear for each life cycle activity. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Quality Management Systems and Process Evaluation/Software Quality Management System Implementation and Evaluation.md)

- The write-up can be expressed in several notations, including natural language, textual lists of [SWEBOK excerpt 06a1aefa5cbd17610943], IDEF0, Petri nets, UML activity diagrams, and BPMN. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Engineering Processes, Lifecycles, and Measurement/Software Process Foundations and Measurement/Software Process Infrastructure Tools and Notations.md)

- Written [SWEBOK excerpt e6878816db2fff24cfe3], whether new developers or automated agents. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Collaboration, Communication, and Cognition in Software Engineering/Writing and Communication in Software Engineering.md)

- The write-up should document relevant facts, significant risks and trade-offs, and any warnings of undesirable consequences from use or misuse. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Professional Responsibility and Intellectual Property in Software Engineering/Documentation and Requirements Trade-off Management/Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)

- The rationale behind key decisions should be recorded, including prior assumptions, alternatives considered, and trade-offs analyzed, so that those who follow or modify the workflow later can understand why choices were made. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Design Concerns, Documentation, and Modeling/Recording Design Rationale for System Maintainability.md)

- The write-up should communicate clearly among all relevant parties, since [SWEBOK excerpt 737f3a6abb9dabdc7278]; it may take the form of texts, diagrams, models, or prototypes. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Design Concerns, Documentation, and Modeling/Software Design Documentation and Communication Methods/Design Documentation and Evaluation/Software Design Descriptions and Communication.md)

- [SWEBOK excerpt 3195bf83cb2eca8378f7]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Professional Responsibility and Intellectual Property in Software Engineering/Documentation and Requirements Trade-off Management/Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md)

- A handoff process between roles must be explicitly put in place, and quality documentation on tasks and all changes must be maintained regardless of organizational structure. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Maintenance Management and Organization/Organizing Software Maintenance Responsibilities/Developer vs. Separate Maintenance Team Trade-offs.md)

- Everything performed in the workflow should be [SWEBOK excerpt 4c6c31852e7a58eb42d3]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Test Generation, Environment Setup, and Incident Management/Test Environment Setup and Controlled Experimentation.md)

- Decisions about which specifications and forms are needed should be made consciously, based on stakeholder audience, subject, and intended usage. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Design Concerns, Documentation, and Modeling/Software Design Documentation and Communication Methods/Design Documentation and Evaluation/Software Design Descriptions and Communication.md)
